correctness.rationale: Every scattered palindromic string of a five-run binary word has 1, 3 or 5 constant runs. The proof partitions these cases and uses min(A,B)=E to avoid overlap in the 0-1-0 family, yielding the full polynomial and exact total. The cubic term E*T*c is bounded by n^3/108 via AM–GM on 2E,2T,c with total at most n. The other terms are O(n^2), and (m,m,2m,m,m) attains the coefficient. Equality rigidity follows from stability of AM–GM and vanishing unused length; all boundary hypotheses are positive. Independent finite enumeration of all distinct subsequences matches the entire polynomial for 1024 tuples (1..4), with length 5..30 finite extrema tested. These finite tests are corroborative, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The five-run restriction is a mathematically natural first cubic-degree threshold, not an arbitrary numerical slice: four-run words cannot realize a five-run palindromic subsequence and have O(n^2) distinct palindromes, while five-run words achieve Theta(n^3). The complete length-spectrum classification and sharp asymptotic constant with unique limiting run proportions resolve the structural extremal question at this threshold. No unproved downstream application is claimed.
